correctness.rationale: The binary de Bruijn graph on order-(d−1) vertices is Eulerian: a cyclic order-d block B of length p=2^d visits each d-word exactly once. Hence for any ℓ>=d, p cyclic phases are distinct. A length-n prefix of B-periodic word contains at least floor((n−ℓ+1)/p) of each phase. With ℓ<=L=floor((n−p+1)/(p+1)), this is >=ℓ+1, so all p phase factors for d<=ℓ<=L qualify. Choose d=floor(0.5log2(n/log2 n)); for n>=64 prove L>=d by a=log2 n<=n/8 and show n−p(L−d+1)<n/p+p(d+1)<3sqrt(n a). Combining lower bound with published Theorem1 M_2(n)<=n yields limit exactly1. Independently an Euler-cycle implementation (different from source FKM recursion) directly counted qualifying binary factors for eight n, verifying each lower bound; no finite experiment proves the limit.
residual_risks: Other classical periodic sequence constructions might already yield a fixed-binary asymptotic extremal result under alternative terminology.
Second-order deficit O(sqrt(n log n)) is only an achievable upper bound, not shown optimal.

evidence: Theorem1 bounds <=n for arbitrary alphabets; Proposition6 asymptotically meets n via r distinct symbols for a word of length r².
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad upper bound and growing-alphabet lower bound do not imply binary lower bound; the latter needs de Bruijn phase-distinguishability.

final_claim: For every n>=64 there exists an explicit binary length-n text with more than n−3 sqrt(n log_2 n) distinct factors whose occurrence count exceeds factor length. Thus fixed-binary maximum M_2(n)/n tends to 1, saturating the published universal <=n bound.
limitations: Uniform explicit bound only n>=64, limiting statement for fixed alphabets >=2.
No exact M_2(n), optimal deficit, or typical random-word result.
